Purpose and scope

This policy sets out Alderbridge Care Group's overarching standard for recruiting and selecting staff fairly,
consistently and safely. It applies to every recruitment at every site and Central Support Office, and sits
above the Safer Recruitment Guidance's own practical, stage-by-stage detail.

Policy statement

Alderbridge recruits on merit, against the genuine requirements of the role, within a process designed to
be fair to every candidate and safe for the people Alderbridge supports, now including a formal fast-track
route for internal mobility and promotion.

Definitions

**Person specification** the essential and desirable criteria a candidate is assessed against for a given
role. **Values-based question bank** the standard set of interview questions probing a candidate's
alignment with Alderbridge's core values. **Internal mobility fast-track** the new, formal process
introduced in this version for an existing staff member applying for internal promotion or lateral movement.
**Extended recruitment timescale** widening the standard timescale for a hard-to-fill role, now requiring
HR Director sign-off rather than the hiring manager's own discretion.

Roles and responsibilities

**The hiring manager** owns their own vacancy from person specification through to onboarding, and
must now obtain HR Director sign-off before widening the recruitment timescale for a hard-to-fill role, a
tightening from the previous version's discretion. **HR** administers the new internal mobility fast-track
process and compiles diversity monitoring data quarterly. **The HR Director** approves or declines a
request to extend a recruitment timescale, a new gate introduced in this version.

1. Write a person specification setting out the essential and desirable criteria for the role.

**HR** administers the new internal mobility fast-track
process and compiles diversity monitoring data quarterly. **The HR Director** approves or declines a
request to extend a recruitment timescale, a new gate introduced in this version.

1. Write a person specification setting out the essential and desirable criteria for the role.

2. Advertise the role, internally and externally as appropriate, unless it qualifies for the internal mobility
fast-track described below.

3. Shortlist applicants against the person specification alone, recording the reasoning for each decision.

4. Interview using a structured format including at least two questions from the values-based question
bank.

5. For a senior role, the hiring manager may opt to include a standardised psychometric assessment.

6. For an existing staff member applying under the internal mobility fast-track, complete the condensed
process set out in the fast-track table below rather than the full external process.

7. Where a role is genuinely hard to fill and a wider timescale is needed, obtain HR Director sign-off before
extending it; this is a new requirement replacing the previous hiring manager discretion.

8. Select the successful candidate, make a conditional offer, and initiate pre-employment checks per the
Safer Recruitment Guidance.

9. Confirm the offer as unconditional only once every required check has been satisfactorily completed.

*Supersedes the version effective 1 April 2025. Escalation changed to also require a call to the supplying pharmacy, not only the on-call manager.*

If the fridge fails

Keep the affected fridge closed, do not move stock on assumption, and call both the on-call manager and the supplying pharmacy (a new requirement — the previous version only required the on-call manager) for advice on whether the stock remains usable; see Immediate containment below for the full response, including when a validated alternative storage location may be used.

Immediate containment

When the medicines-fridge temperature is outside range or the unit fails, staff keep the door closed, note the current and available minimum/maximum readings, label the unit not for use and inform the responsible nurse or manager. Stock is not moved into a domestic refrigerator or discarded on assumption. A validated alternative refrigerator or insulated container is prepared where authorised.

Clinical and pharmacy advice

Staff list every affected medicine, batch where available, storage requirement and estimated exposure time and obtain product-specific pharmacy or manufacturer advice. The decision to use, quarantine or replace each item is recorded. Time-critical doses are escalated so an alternative supply or clinically appropriate plan can be arranged without bypassing prescribing controls.

Recovery and assurance

The failed unit is inspected and must demonstrate a stable compliant temperature before return to service. Quarantined stock remains segregated until a documented decision is made. Temperature records, exposure assessment, advice, stock disposition, engineer report and any omitted-dose or incident record are retained together, and repeated failures trigger equipment replacement review.

Historical development of the medication suite

The medication policy suite has grown incrementally since Alderbridge's founding, beginning with a single combined medication policy that, as the organisation grew and guidance itself became more specific, was gradually separated into the distinct specific policies this overarching document now signposts.

Interfacing with an external pharmacy provider

Alderbridge's contracted pharmacy providers are bound by a service level agreement referencing this overarching policy and its suite, ensuring an external pharmacy's own processes align with Alderbridge's internal standards.

Situation First contact Second contact if unresolved
--- --- ---
Medication error or near miss Registered nurse or senior carer on duty Registered manager
Fridge temperature out of range Senior carer on duty Facilities and Medication Fridge Breakdown Procedure
Suspected covert administration need GP and registered nurse Multidisciplinary team best-interests meeting
Medication-related safeguarding concern Safeguarding Lead directly Registered manager

Resident and family involvement in medication decisions

Wherever a resident has capacity, they are involved directly in decisions about their own medication; where capacity is lacking, family or an advocate is involved in a best-interests process rather than a purely clinical decision being made without any input beyond the care team itself.

Medication reconciliation on admission and transfer

Every resident's full medication list is reconciled against the prescribing GP's own record at admission, and again at any hospital transfer in either direction, since a mismatch between what a resident is believed to be taking and what they are actually prescribed is one of the most common sources of a serious medication error. This reconciliation is completed by a registered nurse or the registered manager, never left solely to an informal handover conversation.

Managing a medication change communicated verbally

Where a GP communicates a medication change verbally, this is confirmed in writing before the change is actually implemented, except in a genuine emergency where immediate action is clinically necessary; a verbal instruction alone is not treated as sufficient authority for an ongoing change to a resident's regular medication regimen.

End of life medication considerations

Medication management at the end of a resident's life often involves a different balance of priorities than routine administration, with comfort and symptom control given particular weight consistent with the End of Life Care Policy; this overarching document's core principles still apply in full, adapted to that different clinical context.

Supersedes the version effective 1 June 2025. Replaces the single central on-call number with a regional on-call structure (three numbers, one per region).

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how staff contact an on-call manager outside of normal hours for a care-related concern requiring senior management input. It applies to every site.

Policy statement

Out of hours, staff call their own region's on-call mobile number (North West, Midlands or South West) — the previous single central number has been decommissioned — providing a reliable route to senior management support with a manager who knows the calling region well.

Definitions

**On-call manager** the senior manager currently holding the on-call rota responsibility for a specific region. **Regional on-call number** one of three mobile numbers, one per region, replacing the previous single central number. **Weekly rota** the rotation within each region's own senior management team, each taking on-call responsibility for one week at a time.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any staff member** on shift calls their own region's on-call number for a genuine out-of-hours concern requiring senior management input. **The regional on-call manager** answers their region's number during their rota week and provides guidance or attends site as the situation requires. **HR** maintains each region's weekly rota and ensures every senior manager knows their upcoming on-call weeks well in advance.

Call your own region's on-call mobile number for any out-of-hours concern requiring senior management input; the previous single central number has been decommissioned and no longer connects.

Give a clear, concise account of the situation to the regional on-call manager who answers, including what has already been done.

Follow the on-call manager's guidance, or arrange for them to attend site if they judge this necessary.

Record the call and its outcome in the site's on-call log.

Supersedes the version effective 1 June 2025. Response time tightened from 10 to 5 working days.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group responds to a reference request for a current or
former staff member. It applies to every reference request received by HR.

Policy statement

HR provides a factual reference confirming dates of employment and job title within 5 working days of a
request, tightened from the previous 10 working days, giving a former or current staff member a faster,
reliable response supporting their next step.

Definitions

**Factual reference** a reference limited to objective facts such as dates of employment and job title, as
distinct from a subjective opinion-based reference. **Reference request** a request received in writing
from a prospective employer or other authorised party, with the staff member's consent where required.

Roles and responsibilities

**HR** processes every reference request and issues the factual reference within the tightened
5-working-day timeframe. **The staff member's line manager** is not the point of contact for a formal
reference request, which is handled centrally by HR to ensure consistency. **The requesting party**
provides sufficient detail, including the staff member's consent where required, for HR to process the
request.

1. Log every reference request on receipt, confirming it includes sufficient detail and any required consent.

2. Issue a factual reference confirming dates of employment and job title within 5 working days of the
request being received, a tightening from the previous 10-working-day standard.

3. Limit the reference to factual, objective information; a subjective opinion on the staff member's
performance or conduct is not included.

4. Direct a request for a fuller, opinion-based reference to the registered manager, who decides whether
and how to respond to that specific, different type of request.

Fraud as explicit external agency routes for a financial abuse concern, aligning with the Safeguarding
Policy (Overarching)'s own formal recognition of financial abuse.

Purpose and scope

This protocol sets out how Alderbridge Care Group works with external agencies to protect a resident from
harm, now explicitly including the agency routes relevant to a financial abuse concern. It applies to every
site and every member of staff.

Policy statement

A safeguarding concern is rarely resolved by Alderbridge acting alone; effective safeguarding depends on
genuine, well-coordinated partnership with external agencies, now explicitly including the Office of the
Public Guardian and Action Fraud for a financial abuse concern, aligning this protocol with the
Safeguarding Policy (Overarching)'s own formal recognition of financial abuse within its suite.

Definitions

**LADO** the Local Authority Designated Officer. **Safeguarding Adults Board (SAB)** the statutory
multi-agency board. **Regional manager liaison role** the coordination function supporting a multi-site or
complex concern. **Office of the Public Guardian** the new external agency route, introduced in this
version, with statutory powers to investigate a concern about an attorney or deputy acting outside their
proper authority. **Action Fraud** the new external route, introduced in this version, for reporting a
suspected fraud against a resident.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any member of staff** reports a safeguarding concern to the registered manager immediately. **The
registered manager** makes the initial external referral decision, now including a financial abuse concern's
specific new routes where relevant. **The organisation-level Safeguarding Lead** coordinates the most
complex situations, including a financial abuse concern requiring Office of the Public Guardian or Action
Fraud involvement, and attends the local Safeguarding Adults Board.

Key Safe Procedure

*Supersedes the Willow-Bank-only version effective 1 February 2025. Extended to cover the whole Midlands Region as community visiting expands to Oakfield Lodge's outreach service.*

Key safe codes

Community support workers across the Midlands Region (not only Willow Bank, as in the prior version) record each client's key safe code in the secure app, never on paper, and report any code change to the office within 24 hours.

Authorisation and coding

A key safe is installed only after property-owner consent, resident or representative agreement where applicable, and a recorded risk assessment. The code is disclosed only to authorised workers who need access and is not written in general notes, visit lists or an unprotected message. Each safe has a unique register entry linked to the address without exposing the code itself.

Use and security

Staff shield the keypad, return the key immediately, scramble the display and confirm the safe has locked before leaving. A missing key, damaged safe, observed code or unexplained access is reported immediately and the premises secured through the agreed contingency route. The code is changed after compromise and at other defined review points.

Review and removal

The responsible manager reviews continuing need, authorised recipients and physical condition at least annually and after a tenancy, care-package or risk change. When the safe is no longer required it is removed or disabled promptly, keys are returned and access records are closed. Installation, code-change, incident, review and removal evidence is retained securely.

Purpose and scope

These guidance notes set out the wellbeing support available to Alderbridge Care Group staff. They apply to every employee, regardless of length of service or role.

Policy statement

Alderbridge recognises that caring for others sustainably requires staff to be genuinely supported themselves, and treats wellbeing support as a proactive, normal part of working life, not something staff must be in crisis to access.

Definitions

**Employee Assistance Programme (EAP)** a confidential, externally provided counselling and support service available to every employee. **Mental health first aider** a colleague trained to provide an initial supportive conversation and signpost further help. **Wellbeing referral** a manager-initiated referral to occupational health where attendance or performance appears affected by a health condition.

Roles and responsibilities

**Every employee** may access the EAP directly and confidentially at any time. **Line managers** notice and respond supportively to a colleague who appears to be struggling, and make a wellbeing referral where appropriate. **Mental health first aiders**, present at every site, provide an initial, non-clinical supportive conversation.

Access the EAP directly, confidentially and free of charge, for telephone counselling or self-help resources, at any time regardless of the reason.

Speak to your site's mental health first aider, listed on the staff noticeboard, for an initial supportive conversation if you are not sure where else to start.

Reasonable adjustments are considered and discussed openly wherever a health condition, physical or mental, affects someone's ability to work as usual.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how a resident's clothing and site linen, and reusable PPE, is laundered at

Policy statement

A resident's own clothing is laundered separately within the barrier system, with a new lost-item tracking
log addressing recurring family concern about missing clothing, and reusable PPE now follows its own

Definitions

**Barrier laundry system** the one-way dirty-to-clean flow protecting against cross-contamination.

dedicated protocol rather than alongside general site linen.

missing item, and follow the new dedicated reusable PPE protocol. **Care staff** identify and bag soiled
linen and reusable PPE separately for correct handling. **The registered manager** reviews the lost-item
tracking log monthly for a recurring pattern.

Laundry Management Procedure

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how a resident's clothing and site linen is laundered at Alderbridge Care Group. It
applies to every site's laundry operation.

Policy statement

A resident's own clothing is laundered separately from site linen, clearly labelled, and washed at a
temperature appropriate to the fabric, while soiled linen follows a specific infection-control hot-wash
standard.

Definitions

**Resident's own clothing** clothing belonging to and worn by an individual resident, laundered separately
and returned to them. **Site linen** bedding, towels and similar items not tied to a specific resident.
**Soiled linen** linen contaminated with a bodily fluid, requiring the infection-control hot-wash standard.

Roles and responsibilities

**Laundry staff** launder a resident's clothing separately, labelled, and follow the correct wash
temperature for the item type. **Care staff** identify and bag soiled linen correctly for separate handling.
**The registered manager** ensures the laundry operation meets this procedure's standard.

1. Label every resident's clothing clearly on admission, and again promptly if a label is lost or becomes
illegible.

2. Launder a resident's own clothing separately from another resident's items and from site linen, at a
temperature appropriate to the fabric.

3. Wash soiled linen at 60 degrees Celsius, following the infection-control hot-wash standard, handled
separately from the point of collection.

4. Return laundered clothing to the correct resident promptly, checking labelling at the point of return.

5. Report a persistent labelling or mix-up issue to the registered manager for investigation.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a specific fabric or garment cannot tolerate the standard wash temperature (for example, a delicate
item), laundry staff use the manufacturer's care label instructions instead, recording the exception so it is
not treated as an error at the next audit.
